# Founder CFO

Your CFO, before any money is spent. The skill gathers the numbers into founder/numbers.json (price, variable cost per unit, fixed monthly costs, startup spend, planned and ramped daily volume, capacity), preferring your own quotes and checkable public prices, with every estimate marked as an estimate and its source noted. It then runs the bundled Python tool, unit_economics.py, which computes the contribution per sale, the real profit margin at the planned volume, the break-even point in units a day, year 1 month by month, the cash needed before the business pays for itself, the payback month for the startup spend, and what-ifs (price -10 percent, volume -20 percent, unit costs +15 percent). The tool flags a price below variable cost, a break-even above capacity, a losing year 1 and a payback beyond 12 months. The skill adds a short CFO note in plain words on top of founder/cfo.md. Not financial, tax or legal advice: the file itself says an accountant should check the structure before money moves.
